title: Million-Dollar Lead Generation — Operator Companion Workbook
subtitle: 6 Printable Operator Worksheets for Enterprise Deal Underwriting, ABM Signal Orchestration, Qualified-Opportunity Economics, Outreach Controls, Delivery Automation, and Small-Team Launch Readiness

worksheets.title: Opportunity, Vertical Underwriting & Counterparty Qualification
worksheets.purpose: Select an enterprise demand-generation niche where observable buying signals, reachable decision makers, and client delivery capacity support repeatable opportunity creation. Separate prospective client contract values from agency revenue, and document the evidence required before accepting an account into the operating pipeline.
instructions: Choose one vertical and one buying problem before purchasing data. Document the expected enterprise procurement sequence, incumbent alternatives, security review requirements, and reasons an economic buyer would authorize a discovery meeting during the next two quarters.

Underwrite the client as carefully as the target account. Review delivery references, existing pipeline, available account executives, cash collection history, and authority to sign your services agreement. Reject assignments whose promised outcomes exceed the client's fulfillment capacity.

Build a small evidence-backed account universe rather than buying an indiscriminate contact list. For every proposed account, capture source date, buying trigger, relevant role, geographic restrictions, and exclusions arising from existing customer relationships or active opportunities.

Define a qualified opportunity through observable acceptance criteria that both parties can inspect. Specify buyer involvement, problem fit, realistic purchasing process, required meeting evidence, and duplicate treatment before quoting any opportunity-based fee to the client.

Score commercial attractiveness and execution friction separately. Use the completed evidence record to choose a narrow pilot, establish client concentration limits, and assign an accountable owner for every unresolved underwriting question before outreach begins.

fields.name: Vertical thesis and enterprise buying problem
fields.prompt: Describe the chosen vertical, expensive operating problem, enterprise purchase category, and observable trigger. Explain why the target buyer would consider a meeting without relying on unsupported savings claims or generic personalization.
fields.example: Target industrial manufacturers with 2,000–15,000 employees replacing fragmented maintenance software. A new plant acquisition or published modernization program supplies the trigger. The client sells deployments worth approximately $1,000,000; our agency earns retainers and accepted-opportunity fees, never the client's implementation contract value.

fields.name: Client identity, authority, and payment capacity
fields.prompt: Identify the contracting entity, authorized signer, billing contact, payment method, and evidence of operating capacity. Record how you verified authority and what collection protection applies before the delivery pod starts work.
fields.example: Northstar Maintenance Software LLC signs through its authorized chief operating officer. Finance confirms the purchase order and an ACH mandate. Two reference calls validate completed enterprise implementations. The agreement requires the first $7,500 retainer before account research and pauses new delivery after documented payment default.

fields.name: Account universe and exclusion boundaries
fields.prompt: Specify account size, industry, location, technology context, and exclusion rules. Quantify the reachable universe after removing existing customers, active opportunities, prohibited territories, and accounts without a defensible reason for contact.
fields.example: Begin with 240 manufacturers identified through company filings and licensed firmographic data. Remove 35 existing customers, 25 active client opportunities, and 20 out-of-territory accounts. The remaining 160 accounts form the research universe; the first pilot uses 40 accounts with dated modernization evidence.

fields.name: Buying committee and access hypothesis
fields.prompt: Map the operational sponsor, economic buyer, technical reviewer, procurement contact, and likely blocker. State which roles must participate initially and which introductions the client must secure after accepting an opportunity.
fields.example: The maintenance director owns the operating problem, the chief operating officer controls program funding, and enterprise IT reviews integrations. Procurement enters after technical fit. An initial meeting requires the director or a delegated program owner; the client account executive must secure executive sponsorship within 30 days.

fields.name: Signal provenance and freshness standard
fields.prompt: Record each trigger's source, observation date, account match, permitted use, and expiration rule. Distinguish verified company events from inferred intent, and identify evidence that would invalidate the proposed outreach hypothesis.
fields.example: A manufacturer announced a plant acquisition 18 days ago on its investor-relations website. Store the URL, publication date, and relevant excerpt in HubSpot. Refresh the trigger after 30 days. Treat third-party topic interest as directional research, not proof that a named person requested contact.

fields.name: Qualified-opportunity acceptance definition
fields.prompt: Write the minimum evidence for an accepted opportunity, including account eligibility, participant role, confirmed problem, meeting attendance, and next step. Identify conditions that create research leads but do not earn opportunity fees.
fields.example: An accepted opportunity requires an eligible account, an attended 30-minute discovery meeting with a maintenance program owner, a documented modernization problem, and agreement to a technical follow-up. A calendar booking alone earns no fee. A student researcher, vendor solicitation, or unrelated inquiry fails qualification.

fields.name: Client fulfillment and sales capacity
fields.prompt: Measure the client's ability to respond, conduct discovery, supply technical support, and fulfill resulting contracts. Set maximum weekly introductions and response deadlines so your delivery does not overwhelm the client's available selling resources.
fields.example: The client assigns two account executives and one solutions engineer. Together they can handle four new discovery meetings weekly and two technical workshops. The response commitment is one business day. Reduce introductions when more than six accepted opportunities lack a documented next action.

fields.name: Sales-cycle and procurement friction map
fields.prompt: Estimate the sequence and duration of discovery, technical validation, security review, procurement, and contracting. Separate the agency's first client-sale timeline from the client's downstream enterprise buying cycle and resulting cash receipts.
fields.example: Plan 3–12 months to win the agency's first client. For that client's prospects, model 30 days of discovery, 60 days of technical validation, and another 90–180 days for procurement. Agency fees follow contracted service and acceptance milestones, rather than waiting for the enterprise deployment to close.

fields.name: Concentration and counterparty exposure
fields.prompt: Calculate revenue exposure by client, vertical, and payment status. State a practical concentration threshold, explain temporary launch exceptions, and define the action required when one counterparty becomes essential to payroll coverage.
fields.example: At the Base case, six equally productive clients each generate $112,500 annually, representing 16.67% of $675,000 revenue. Set a mature-book limit of 25% per client. During the one-client launch, maintain a separate cash runway and prospect pipeline rather than describing concentration as diversified.

fields.name: Underwriting decision and pilot boundary
fields.prompt: Summarize the decision, supporting evidence, unresolved conditions, pilot scope, and accountable owner. Include the canonical candidate score without treating its aggregate ranking as evidence that a particular client or account will perform.
fields.example: Proceed with a 40-account pilot after signer verification and CRM exclusion matching. Candidate #21 carries an 86/100 Money-to-Manpower Score and pipeline rank #18 of 29. Its component scores are 24 revenue, 21 margin, 16 team efficiency, 9 startup accessibility, and 12 automation.

worksheets.completion_gate: The commercial lead signs a dated underwriting record containing verified client authority, 40 evidence-backed pilot accounts, written opportunity acceptance criteria, delivery capacity, and named owners for every unresolved condition; excluded accounts cannot enter outreach.

worksheets.title: Unit Economics, Scrub Reserve & Working-Capital Float Calculator
worksheets.purpose: Translate retainers and qualified-opportunity fees into reconciled operator economics. Model rejected submissions, cash reserves, collection delays, and staffing without counting client contract values as agency revenue. Test whether available startup capital can support the actual sales cycle and delivery commitments.
instructions: Enter the three canonical annual scenarios before building a monthly forecast. Preserve their exact revenue, owner profit, margin, and staffing figures. Treat the illustrated client counts and fee combinations as operating bridges, not additional canonical assumptions.

Separate submitted opportunities, accepted opportunities, invoiced fees, recognized revenue, and collected cash. Calculate scrub rates on submitted records and document the accounting treatment of rejected submissions, service credits, advance retainers, and temporary cash reserves.

Assign every annual operating cost to one category and reconcile the total to the scenario margin. Include employee costs, contractor delivery, acquisition, software, data, administration, and rework without deducting an internal reserve allocation as another expense.

Build a collection calendar that reflects actual contract terms. Model advance retainers separately from opportunity invoices, calculate average receivables, and identify the lowest projected cash balance before committing to additional payroll or annual software contracts.

Stress the plan for delayed client acquisition, a rejected opportunity batch, and loss of the largest client. Where funding is insufficient, reduce fixed commitments or secure documented funding rather than assuming enterprise deals close earlier.

fields.name: Conservative scenario revenue bridge
fields.prompt: Reconstruct Conservative annual operator revenue from a specific retainer and accepted-opportunity mix. Reconcile costs, owner profit, margin, and team composition while keeping downstream enterprise contract values outside the agency revenue calculation.
fields.example: Three clients paying $3,500 monthly generate $126,000 annual retainers. Another 24 accepted opportunities at $1,000 produce $24,000. Total revenue is $150,000; annual costs are $120,000, leaving $30,000 owner net profit at 20% margin. The canonical team is 2 FT + 3 C.

fields.name: Base scenario revenue bridge
fields.prompt: Construct a Base annual revenue bridge with client count, monthly retainer, accepted-opportunity volume, and fee. Show the annual and monthly averages, then reconcile owner profit and the required canonical staffing configuration.
fields.example: Six clients at $7,500 monthly produce $540,000 retainers. Ninety accepted opportunities at $1,500 add $135,000. Annual revenue totals $675,000, averaging $56,250 monthly. Costs of $472,500 leave $202,500 owner net profit at 30.0% margin with 2 FT + 3 C.

fields.name: Scaled small-team revenue bridge
fields.prompt: Build the Scaled revenue bridge without increasing the canonical seven-person team. Explain the client and opportunity volumes supporting annual revenue, and reconcile all-in costs and owner profit to the required net margin.
fields.example: Eight clients paying $10,000 monthly generate $960,000 retainers. Another 120 accepted opportunities at $2,000 add $240,000. Revenue reaches $1,200,000; costs total $720,000, leaving $480,000 owner net profit at 40% margin. Staffing is 3 FT + 4 C, totaling seven people.

fields.name: Base expense allocation and capacity assumptions
fields.prompt: Allocate the Base annual expense ceiling across named operating categories. Specify contractor availability and employee assumptions, and identify any market wage or delivery constraint that would make the canonical margin unattainable locally.
fields.example: Allocate $168,000 to loaded employee costs, $120,000 to three fractional contractors, $36,000 to software, $48,000 to data, $24,500 to administration and insurance, $48,000 to acquisition, and $28,000 to delivery rework. Total costs equal $472,500; validate local compensation before hiring against this illustration.

fields.name: Submission scrub and accepted-fee yield
fields.prompt: Calculate submitted volume, rejected volume, accepted volume, scrub percentage, and earned opportunity fees. Distinguish pre-acceptance defects from post-recognition credits so the same rejected opportunity cannot reduce revenue twice in the model.
fields.example: Submit 100 opportunities during the Base year and reject 10 for duplicates or missing qualification evidence. The 10% scrub leaves 90 accepted opportunities earning $135,000. The rejected submissions represent $15,000 of unearned potential fees, not recognized revenue and not an additional expense.

fields.name: Defect cash reserve and credit treatment
fields.prompt: Set an internal cash reserve for disputed fees and remedial delivery. Explain whether each reserve movement affects cash availability, recognized revenue, or operating expense, and state how actual credits change the forecast.
fields.example: Earmark 10% of the Base year's $135,000 accepted-opportunity fees, or $13,500, as an internal cash reserve. This transfer does not reduce the $202,500 canonical profit. If a $1,500 credit becomes valid, record its actual treatment and publish a separate revised forecast rather than hiding the variance.

fields.name: Receivables float and collection timing
fields.prompt: Specify retainer collection dates, opportunity invoice terms, expected payment delay, and average receivables. Separate earned service revenue from advance cash receipts, and identify which cash balances remain unavailable for owner distributions.
fields.example: Collect $45,000 of monthly Base retainers in advance and recognize them as services are delivered. Average monthly opportunity fees are $11,250. At 45-day collection timing, using a 30-day planning month, opportunity receivables average $16,875. Retain additional cash for payroll, taxes, and disputed invoices.

fields.name: Startup capital and pre-revenue runway
fields.prompt: Choose a startup funding amount within the supplied range, itemize initial commitments, and calculate runway without client receipts. Compare that runway with the 3–12 month first-deal window and identify the financing shortfall explicitly.
fields.example: Start with $75,000, within the $15,000–$100,000 capital range. Spend $25,000 on setup and retain $50,000 cash. At $12,500 monthly pre-revenue burn, runway is four months. Twelve months would require $175,000 including setup, leaving a $100,000 shortfall against this funding plan.

fields.name: Operating range and mature cash buffer
fields.prompt: Compare the supplied monthly operating range with each scenario's implied all-in costs. Do not force mature payroll into an incompatible startup budget; document staged staffing and the cash buffer required at the selected run rate.
fields.example: The supplied monthly opex range is $4,000–$20,000, but Base all-in costs average $39,375 and Scaled costs average $60,000. Treat this as a planning mismatch requiring staged commitments. A three-month Base cost buffer is $118,125, already exceeding the $100,000 upper startup-capital figure.

fields.name: Concentration stress and break-even sensitivity
fields.prompt: Remove the largest client's revenue while initially holding costs constant. Calculate remaining profit and margin, then identify specific reducible commitments and the time required to restore the planned earnings level.
fields.example: Losing one equal Base client removes $112,500 annual revenue. With costs initially unchanged at $472,500, revenue falls to $562,500 and profit to $90,000, a 16% margin. Recovering the original profit requires replacing that revenue or reducing actual costs, not merely reallocating the cash reserve.

worksheets.completion_gate: The operator and finance owner reconcile all three canonical scenarios, document scrub and reserve treatments, and approve a dated cash forecast showing funding sources for committed spending through the next client-acquisition milestone.

worksheets.title: Execution, Opportunity Ledger & Technical QA Pre-Flight
worksheets.purpose: Create an auditable delivery path from source evidence to client acceptance and payment. Establish identifiers, ownership rules, attribution records, technical checks, and dispute procedures that prevent duplicate billing, unsupported qualification, lost handoffs, and accidental exposure of one client's account data to another.
instructions: Map the workflow before configuring integrations. Give each stage an entry condition, required evidence, accountable owner, and permitted next state. Prevent a booked meeting from automatically becoming an accepted opportunity or a billable ledger entry.

Configure stable identifiers and client boundaries across the CRM, scheduling system, evidence store, and billing export. Test duplicates and existing opportunities using the client's actual suppression snapshot before importing the first production account batch.

Write the attribution policy into the services schedule and mirror it in the ledger. Record first qualifying touch, pre-existing opportunity status, acceptance evidence, and exceptions so later disputes can be resolved from records rather than recollection.

Perform a complete synthetic journey using records controlled by the delivery team. Validate permissions, message rendering, calendar time zones, rescheduling, cancellation, event retries, fee eligibility, and the exact evidence attached to the client's acceptance request.

Reconcile CRM acceptance counts, invoice lines, credits, and cash receipts before each billing run. Assign unresolved differences to named owners, retain an exception log, and block duplicate or unsupported fee lines while continuing valid delivery.

fields.name: Execution stages and state transitions
fields.prompt: Define the ordered operational states from account research through collection. Identify evidence required for each transition, and specify which state changes require human review instead of automatic promotion by an integration.
fields.example: Use Researched, Eligible, Contacted, Engaged, Booked, Attended, Submitted, Accepted, Invoiced, and Collected states. An attendance record moves Booked to Attended; a qualification packet moves Attended to Submitted. Only recorded client acceptance permits Accepted status. Calendar events cannot create invoice lines without that acceptance.

fields.name: Stable identifiers and client isolation
fields.prompt: Specify identifiers for clients, accounts, contacts, meetings, opportunities, and invoices. Explain how access controls and matching rules prevent cross-client exposure or duplicate fees when names, domains, or meeting times change.
fields.example: Assign client_id C006, account_id A0142, and opportunity_id O006-0142-01. Use the CRM object ID as the durable contact reference rather than an email address alone. Separate client workspaces and permissions. A rescheduled meeting retains its opportunity ID and cannot create a second billable opportunity.

fields.name: Source evidence and qualification packet
fields.prompt: List the evidence attached to each submitted opportunity, including trigger provenance, participant role, attendance, confirmed problem, and agreed next action. Limit captured personal information to what delivery and dispute resolution actually require.
fields.example: Opportunity O006-0142-01 includes the dated acquisition announcement, participant job title, meeting attendance confirmation, structured discovery notes, and a technical workshop date. Store restricted notes in the client workspace. Do not attach unrelated personal profiles or a full meeting recording when concise evidence is sufficient.

fields.name: Attribution window and pre-existing pipeline
fields.prompt: Write the attribution window, baseline pipeline check, duplicate hierarchy, and exception process. Distinguish contractual fee attribution from claims about causal impact on client revenue or influence across the entire buying committee.
fields.example: The contract attributes eligible opportunities submitted within 90 days of the agency's documented qualifying touch. Exclude opportunities already active in the client's kickoff snapshot. For overlapping sources, use the signed exception schedule. This rule determines the $1,500 fee; it does not establish that the agency caused the client's entire sale.

fields.name: Acceptance deadline and dispute packet
fields.prompt: Define the client's review period, valid rejection reasons, required rejection evidence, and escalation owner. State whether silence has contractual effect and how disputed records are withheld from billing during investigation.
fields.example: Give the client five business days to accept or reject a complete submission. Require a reason code and supporting CRM record for duplicates. Silence leaves the submission pending under this contract. Escalate overdue reviews to the sales operations lead; disputed opportunities remain outside the accepted-fee invoice batch.

fields.name: Opportunity and invoice ledger columns
fields.prompt: Specify the minimum ledger columns connecting operational events with financial records. Include immutable references, amounts, dates, status, credits, and cash application so a reviewer can reconstruct one opportunity without searching unrelated systems.
fields.example: Record client ID, opportunity ID, submitted date, accepted date, fee amount, invoice ID, invoice date, due date, credit reference, payment date, and applied cash. O006-0142-01 earns $1,500 on acceptance, appears once on invoice I006-004, and closes only when its payment allocation is recorded.

fields.name: Scheduling and handoff quality checks
fields.prompt: Describe calendar ownership, time-zone handling, invite content, reminder behavior, cancellation rules, and client handoff requirements. Include checks that distinguish actual attendance from accepted invitations or automated calendar responses.
fields.example: Calendly routes the meeting to the assigned account executive and displays the buyer's local time zone. The invitation states the discussion topic and includes cancellation links. A controlled test checks daylight-saving behavior. The account executive confirms attendance manually; an accepted invitation does not satisfy the attended-meeting requirement.

fields.name: Idempotency, retries, and event ordering
fields.prompt: Define event identifiers, deduplication storage, retry limits, and rules for late or out-of-order updates. Explain how the system handles a cancellation arriving after booking and prevents repeated webhook delivery from creating extra fees.
fields.example: Persist each provider event ID before processing its effects. A repeated meeting-created webhook returns the existing result. Retry transient failures three times, then send the record to a review queue. A later cancellation changes meeting status but never deletes the audit history or silently reverses an accepted invoice.

fields.name: Pre-flight test cases and expected results
fields.prompt: List representative test cases with expected outcomes and evidence locations. Cover successful delivery, suppression, duplicates, cancellations, access isolation, and billing errors before connecting production lists or sending messages to external recipients.
fields.example: Run 12 controlled cases: four valid journeys, two suppressed contacts, two duplicates, one cancellation, one failed handoff, one cross-client access attempt, and one repeated invoice export. Expect four eligible submissions, zero suppressed sends, zero duplicate fees, and denied cross-client access. Store results beside the configuration version.

fields.name: Monthly reconciliation and correction ownership
fields.prompt: Describe the reconciliation between accepted opportunities, invoice lines, credits, and receipts. Assign correction owners and deadlines, and require an explanatory record for differences rather than editing historical totals to force agreement.
fields.example: April contains eight accepted opportunities at $1,500, totaling $12,000. The draft export contains nine fee lines, or $13,500. Finance removes the duplicate line before issuance and records the integration defect. Retainers reconcile separately to $45,000; cash receipts follow payment timing rather than the acceptance count.

worksheets.completion_gate: The delivery lead records passing results for all 12 controlled cases, verifies client isolation and duplicate prevention, and demonstrates a complete source-to-payment audit trail without sending production outreach or issuing unsupported invoices.

worksheets.title: Statutory, Licensing, Contract & Outreach Audit
worksheets.purpose: Translate jurisdiction, communication channel, data provenance, and compensation structure into concrete operating requirements. Identify when ordinary enterprise marketing crosses into regulated referral activity, establish enforceable contract boundaries, and maintain evidence that outreach and data handling follow the rules applicable to each campaign.
instructions: Inventory recipient locations, channels, data sources, and the actual service being promoted. Evaluate requirements for each combination rather than assuming a business email address, public profile, or enterprise buyer removes all privacy and outreach obligations.

Document the relevant statutory provisions and operational controls together. Identify the responsible reviewer, evidence retained, refresh date, and conditions that stop a campaign. Resolve uncertain channel or sector classifications before paying for production distribution.

Review the compensation model independently from the message content. A fixed retainer, accepted-meeting fee, percentage commission, and transaction-contingent payment can receive different treatment, particularly in healthcare, settlement services, securities, and federal procurement.

Make the services agreement match the operating ledger. Specify qualification, attribution, acceptance, rejection evidence, credits, payment timing, data responsibilities, confidentiality, and termination exports so neither party must invent commercial rules after a disputed introduction.

Test suppression, rights requests, incident escalation, and vendor access using controlled records. Retain proof of the tests and unresolved findings. A written policy is insufficient when the sending platform or contractor workflow bypasses its requirements.

fields.name: Jurisdiction and channel applicability register
fields.prompt: List sender and recipient locations, intended channels, recipient categories, and promoted services. Explain the method used to determine applicable rules and identify campaign combinations that require additional review before any contact.
fields.example: The initial campaign uses email to United States manufacturing employees and excludes SMS, automated voice, personal mobile numbers, and European recipients. Record state locations where available. A proposed United Kingdom expansion receives a separate PECR and UK GDPR review before records enter the sending segment.

fields.name: Commercial email requirements and suppression
fields.prompt: Translate commercial email requirements into message, sender, address, and opt-out controls. Identify the applicable statute, the operational deadline, and how suppression propagates across client campaigns, vendors, and future list imports.
fields.example: Apply 15 U.S.C. § 7704 and 16 CFR Part 316: use accurate headers, nondeceptive subjects, required advertising identification, a valid postal address, and a clear opt-out. Honor requests within 10 business days; operationally suppress immediately. Test that later imports cannot reactivate the same opted-out address.

fields.name: Telephone, text, and recording restrictions
fields.prompt: Identify any calling, texting, prerecorded content, automated dialing, or recording planned for the campaign. Document applicable consent and do-not-call requirements, relevant state overlays, and proof required before enabling each channel.
fields.example: Keep automated telemarketing calls and texts disabled until 47 U.S.C. § 227, 47 CFR § 64.1200, and applicable state requirements are evaluated for the specific technology and recipients. Maintain required consent evidence. Evaluate California Penal Code § 632 before recording confidential conversations involving California participants.

fields.name: Privacy roles, notices, and individual rights
fields.prompt: Determine whether the agency and client act as controllers, processors, businesses, service providers, or another defined role. Identify applicable thresholds, notices, rights handling, and contractual restrictions rather than assuming business contacts are categorically exempt.
fields.example: For covered California activity, assess Civil Code §§ 1798.100–1798.199.100, including notice and applicable rights duties; business-contact data is not categorically outside the statute. For EU expansion, document GDPR Articles 6, 14, and 21 analysis. A claimed legitimate interest does not automatically authorize every outreach channel.

fields.name: Data sourcing and broker status assessment
fields.prompt: Document where contact data originates, contractual use rights, refresh methods, and whether the business sells personal information outside a direct relationship. Assess registration and deletion duties where the actual business model triggers them.
fields.example: The agency licenses 800 business-contact records for a named campaign and records permitted uses and deletion terms. Before offering standalone contact files to other buyers, assess California Civil Code §§ 1798.99.80–1798.99.89 and current implementing requirements. Do not assume that calling the product research removes data-broker obligations.

fields.name: Healthcare, property, and securities fee restrictions
fields.prompt: Screen the promoted service and payment trigger for sector-specific referral restrictions. Identify any transaction-linked compensation, licensing question, or covered service that requires restructuring or specialist review before accepting the engagement.
fields.example: Exclude healthcare-program referrals pending review under 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b), settlement-service referrals under 12 U.S.C. § 2607, and securities introductions implicating 15 U.S.C. § 78o(a). A $2,000 fee labeled marketing can still create a substantive issue when payment depends on a regulated referral.

fields.name: Federal procurement contingent-fee screening
fields.prompt: Identify campaigns involving federal contract opportunities and compensation tied to awards. Review relevant contract clauses and exceptions, and distinguish ordinary enterprise demand generation from conduct involving procurement influence or restricted payments.
fields.example: A prospect requests 2% of any resulting federal software award. Review FAR Subpart 3.4 and FAR 52.203-5, including the facts supporting any bona fide employee or established commercial selling agency exception. Do not launch the award-linked arrangement merely because the client proposes calling it a lead fee.

fields.name: Services agreement and fee schedule
fields.prompt: Draft the commercial clauses controlling scope, retainer earning, opportunity acceptance, attribution, credits, payment deadlines, and termination. Ensure the written terms match the CRM workflow and avoid promising client sales outcomes outside your control.
fields.example: Schedule A states a $7,500 monthly retainer and $1,500 per accepted opportunity, payable within 30 days of invoice. It incorporates qualification criteria, the 90-day attribution window, five-business-day review, and evidence-based rejection. Client contract values are excluded from agency fees; termination requires an agreed data export and retention schedule.

fields.name: Security, retention, and incident ownership
fields.prompt: Specify access roles, authentication, encryption, retention, vendor restrictions, and incident escalation. Connect retention periods to operational or contractual needs, while preserving minimal suppression information needed to avoid contacting people who opted out.
fields.example: Require multifactor authentication for HubSpot and Google Workspace, restrict exports to two named administrators, and review contractor access monthly. Delete rejected research records after 90 days under the documented schedule, subject to holds. Retain minimal suppression identifiers with restricted access so later imports do not restart outreach.

fields.name: Audit findings and remediation evidence
fields.prompt: Record each finding, affected campaign, severity, accountable owner, target date, and verification evidence. Specify which defects prevent sending or payment, and close findings only after an observed test confirms the required control works.
fields.example: Finding P-03 shows that a contractor CSV import bypasses suppression matching. Pause that import path and assign the CRM administrator a two-day repair deadline. Retest 20 controlled records, including five suppressed addresses. Close the finding only when all five remain excluded and the result is attached.

worksheets.completion_gate: The responsible reviewer records the applicable channel and sector requirements, the client signs matching commercial terms, and controlled tests verify suppression and access restrictions. Unresolved regulated-fee questions remain outside the active campaign.

worksheets.title: Automation, Outbound Growth & Risk Fallback Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Automate account qualification, CRM attribution, and scheduling without automating unsupported claims or disputed fee decisions. Connect account signals to bounded experiments, measurable funnel improvement, and tested manual fallbacks so a small delivery team can expand capacity while preserving evidence quality and client trust.
instructions: Draw the automation path from approved data sources to account scoring, outreach, replies, scheduling, qualification, and billing. Mark every point where a machine inference must remain provisional until supported by evidence or reviewed by an accountable person.

Start with the three canonical leverage points: account qualification, CRM attribution, and meeting scheduling. Measure minutes saved and errors introduced for each automation before expanding it to additional clients, channels, or more sensitive data categories.

Design outbound experiments around a specific account hypothesis and useful message. Change one meaningful variable at a time, preserve comparison cohorts, and judge performance using accepted opportunities and downstream quality rather than email opens alone.

Set service-health thresholds that protect recipients and delivery quality. Investigate bounces, complaints, permission failures, and unusual acceptance changes. Do not respond to a broken or restricted channel by disguising identity or bypassing provider controls.

Rehearse manual fallback for data-provider failure, CRM outage, calendar errors, and staff absence. Specify who can pause sends, how pending work is preserved, and how recovered systems reconcile events without duplicating meetings or opportunity fees.

fields.name: Automation architecture and system ownership
fields.prompt: Map the systems used for account research, CRM records, outreach, scheduling, and billing export. Assign an owner to each integration and explain which system is authoritative for qualification, acceptance, suppression, and payment status.
fields.example: Use licensed data and company websites for research, HubSpot for account and opportunity state, a permitted business-email platform for outreach, and Calendly for scheduling. Finance controls invoice issuance. The CRM administrator owns integrations; HubSpot acceptance records, not calendar bookings, authorize opportunity-fee export.

fields.name: Account qualification scoring and explainability
fields.prompt: Define account-level scoring inputs, weights, minimum evidence, and exclusion overrides. Require a readable reason for each score and prevent weak inferred signals from overriding contractual exclusions or explicit recipient preferences.
fields.example: Score firmographic fit at 40 points, a verified modernization trigger at 35, and identified relevant roles at 25. Research accounts scoring at least 75. An existing active opportunity or suppression match overrides the score. Record the source behind each component so reviewers can challenge stale or mismatched evidence.

fields.name: AI-assisted research and message review
fields.prompt: Describe permitted machine assistance, source requirements, human review, and data minimization. Specify how unsupported claims, mistaken identities, sensitive inferences, and invented buying intent are detected before generated text reaches a recipient.
fields.example: A language model drafts a 90-word message from approved company facts and the client positioning brief. A researcher checks every factual sentence against its source. Reject invented budget claims and statements that a named person visited a website. Send only reviewed drafts through the normal suppression-controlled workflow.

fields.name: Outbound cohort and experiment design
fields.prompt: Define the experiment hypothesis, account cohorts, message difference, observation period, and success metric. Keep contact pressure controlled, and identify confounders that would make apparent performance differences unsuitable for broad deployment.
fields.example: Split 80 eligible accounts into two matched groups of 40. Variant A leads with acquisition integration; Variant B leads with maintenance visibility. Use the same offer and role coverage for 21 days. Compare positive replies and accepted opportunities, while acknowledging that small counts provide limited statistical precision.

fields.name: Funnel math and accepted-opportunity target
fields.prompt: Translate account coverage into delivered contacts, positive replies, held meetings, submissions, and accepted opportunities. Use consistent denominators and connect the resulting annual accepted volume to the Base fee model rather than client contract values.
fields.example: Across six clients, contact 1,200 distinct eligible people annually. At 20% positive replies, obtain 240 conversations; 50% meeting conversion yields 120 held meetings. Submit 100 qualified records and accept 90 after scrub. Those 90 accepted opportunities generate $135,000 at the Base $1,500 fee.

fields.name: Sender health and recipient protection thresholds
fields.prompt: Set monitoring thresholds for bounce rates, complaints, opt-outs, and authentication failures. Explain the investigation and pause procedure, including how small sample sizes and provider-specific requirements affect decisions about continuing a campaign.
fields.example: Verify SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment before sending. Pause a batch when hard bounces exceed 2% or any complaint suggests a sourcing defect; investigate even one complaint in a small pilot. These are internal thresholds, not provider entitlements. Repair sourcing and permissions instead of cycling identities.

fields.name: CRM attribution automation and reconciliation
fields.prompt: Describe how touch events, baseline exclusions, attribution windows, and acceptance decisions populate CRM records. Specify exception handling and the checks that prevent automatic attribution from becoming unsupported billing or exaggerated revenue influence claims.
fields.example: A workflow stamps the first qualifying touch and checks the 90-day attribution window against the kickoff pipeline snapshot. Conflicting source records enter a review queue. The automation proposes attribution but cannot mark client acceptance. Weekly reconciliation compares accepted opportunity IDs with exported fee lines and flags unmatched records.

fields.name: Scheduling leverage and human capacity
fields.prompt: Estimate scheduling workload before and after automation, including exceptions and no-shows. Translate time saved into available delivery capacity, and identify the human judgment that must remain outside calendar routing and reminder automation.
fields.example: At 120 held meetings annually, manual scheduling averaging 20 minutes consumes 40 hours. Automated routing plus five minutes of exception handling per meeting consumes 10 hours, freeing 30 hours. Staff still verify role fit and attendance; automated reminders do not establish qualification or justify an opportunity fee.

fields.name: Outage fallback and restart reconciliation
fields.prompt: Define the manual process for unavailable CRM, scheduling, data, or sending systems. Identify pause authority, temporary records, access restrictions, and the reconciliation steps required before restarting automation after service restoration.
fields.example: If HubSpot is unavailable, pause new outreach and fee exports. The delivery lead tracks existing meeting changes in an access-restricted worksheet using durable opportunity IDs. After recovery, compare timestamps and event IDs before replaying updates. Resume only after pending cancellations and suppression changes have synchronized.

fields.name: Growth flywheel and dependency risk
fields.prompt: Explain how validated delivery evidence improves targeting, positioning, referrals, and retention. List vendor and client dependencies, assign fallback owners, and prevent case-study production from exposing confidential client pipeline or implying unverified closed revenue.
fields.example: Each month, summarize accepted-opportunity reasons and rejection patterns to improve the next account cohort. Request client permission before publishing a case study showing 15 accepted opportunities. Report client sales outcomes only when verified and authorized. Maintain portable CRM exports and an alternate licensed data source to reduce dependency.

worksheets.completion_gate: The automation owner demonstrates qualification scoring, attribution review, scheduling, immediate suppression, and a successful outage recovery using controlled records. The growth lead approves one bounded experiment with defined denominators and documented pause criteria.

worksheets.title: 30-Day Launch Sprint, Pod KPI Scorecard & Exit-Readiness Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Turn the operating design into a funded 30-day launch plan with clear responsibilities, evidence-based milestones, and explicit stop decisions. Track the small team's delivery quality and financial health while organizing transferable contracts, clean records, and documented processes for eventual ownership transition.
instructions: Treat the first 30 days as a readiness and learning sprint, not a substitute for the stated 3–12 month first-deal timeline. Set milestones around validated accounts, contract terms, controlled tests, and qualified client conversations rather than assumed collections.

Assign every deliverable to one accountable person and identify supporting contractors. Preserve the canonical team structure when describing steady-state scenarios, but stage launch commitments according to available cash and verified demand rather than hiring everyone immediately.

Use one weekly scorecard combining leading indicators, accepted-opportunity quality, collections, cash runway, and client concentration. Define each denominator and source system so the pod cannot improve an apparent metric by changing its interpretation between reviews.

Maintain a decision log for changes to niche, pricing, targeting, staffing, and automation. Record the evidence behind each change and its expected cash impact. Separate deviations from the forecast from revisions to the immutable canonical scenario reference.

Build transfer readiness while operating, not after receiving an acquisition inquiry. Keep signed agreements, reconciled financials, access inventories, documented procedures, and client permissions organized, while restricting confidential information until a legitimate transaction process authorizes disclosure.

fields.name: Days 1–7 underwriting and commercial foundation
fields.prompt: Specify first-week deliverables, owners, spending limits, and evidence required for completion. Focus on selecting the vertical, validating the offer, preparing contract terms, and reconciling the cash plan before configuring extensive automation.
fields.example: The commercial lead completes five client-discovery interviews and selects manufacturing modernization. The delivery lead researches 40 pilot accounts. Finance reconciles the $75,000 funding plan and limits week-one commitments to $5,000 within the $25,000 setup budget. Completion requires an evidence-backed offer and reviewed services schedule.

fields.name: Days 8–14 data, systems, and controlled tests
fields.prompt: List second-week system configuration and verification work, including access roles, suppression, identifiers, attribution, scheduling, and billing exports. Require observable test results rather than treating installed software or purchased data as completed operational capability.
fields.example: Configure the HubSpot stages, client access boundaries, Calendly routing, and acceptance ledger. Run the 12 controlled pre-flight cases and repair every fee-duplication or suppression defect. Import only the 40 researched pilot accounts after exclusion matching. Keep production outreach disabled until the operational and channel checks are complete.

fields.name: Days 15–21 bounded client-acquisition experiment
fields.prompt: Define the third-week acquisition experiment, target counterparties, contact limits, measurement period, and review owner. Distinguish selling the agency service from performing outbound work for an unsigned client or claiming a downstream enterprise deal.
fields.example: Approach 20 carefully selected software vendors that serve the chosen manufacturing segment, using the approved email controls. Target four substantive sales conversations as a learning objective. Present the $7,500 retainer and $1,500 accepted-opportunity structure. Do not launch client-branded campaigns before a signed agreement and required funding.

fields.name: Days 22–30 review and next-month decision
fields.prompt: Set the final-week review agenda, continuation criteria, budget decision, and unresolved evidence requirements. Explain how the operator proceeds if the sprint produces learning and qualified conversations but no signed client or collected revenue.
fields.example: Review interview evidence, contact quality, reply reasons, test results, and actual cash spending. If no client has signed, preserve the 3–12 month acquisition assumption and authorize only the next funded experiment. Continue with the niche when buyers validate the problem; revise positioning when objections consistently reject the proposed value.

fields.name: Pod roles and staged staffing commitments
fields.prompt: Assign commercial, research, operations, quality, and finance responsibilities across employees and contractors. Document fractional availability, backup coverage, and the revenue or cash milestones required before increasing fixed commitments toward the canonical team.
fields.example: At Base steady state, two full-time roles cover commercial leadership and delivery operations. Three fractional contractors cover research, CRM automation, and finance support. During launch, use limited contracted hours until funding supports recurring commitments. The Scaled structure adds one full-time client lead and one contractor, reaching seven people.

fields.name: Weekly pod KPI definitions and evidence
fields.prompt: Define the weekly metrics, denominators, owners, and source records. Include delivery quality, client response speed, overdue reviews, collection performance, and cash runway so volume metrics cannot hide rejection problems or deteriorating liquidity.
fields.example: Track eligible accounts researched, positive replies per delivered contact, held meetings per scheduled meeting, accepted opportunities per submission, overdue acceptance reviews, and collected cash per due invoice dollar. Finance reports runway from unrestricted cash and forecast net burn; the delivery lead reports rejection reasons by client every Friday.

fields.name: Monthly financial scorecard and variance bridge
fields.prompt: Compare actual revenue, costs, owner profit, and collections with the chosen scenario run rate. Separate timing differences from structural shortfalls and explain each material variance using ledger evidence rather than changing the reference scenario.
fields.example: The Base monthly average is $56,250 revenue, $39,375 costs, and $16,875 owner net profit. A month with $45,000 retainers and eight accepted opportunities produces $57,000 revenue. At $39,375 costs, profit is $17,625, or $750 above the reference; cash may differ because fees collect later.

fields.name: Stop, repair, and expansion decision log
fields.prompt: Write specific conditions for pausing outreach, repairing delivery, changing the offer, or adding capacity. Include decision authority and cash consequences, and distinguish a failed experiment from evidence that the entire business model cannot work.
fields.example: Pause a client's new submissions if two consecutive batches exceed 20% rejection and investigate qualification drift. Freeze hiring when forecast cash falls below eight weeks of committed spending. Expand account coverage only after acceptance quality stabilizes and the client confirms sales capacity. Record each decision with an owner and review date.

fields.name: Transferable operating assets and rights ledger
fields.prompt: Inventory contracts, process documents, domains, system configurations, data rights, and staff knowledge that a successor would need. Identify assignment restrictions, client permissions, and vendor limitations before describing the business as readily transferable.
fields.example: Maintain signed client agreements, renewal dates, assignment clauses, domain ownership records, CRM configuration exports, and documented qualification procedures. Flag two data licenses requiring vendor permission before transfer. Store contractor confidentiality and intellectual-property terms with each engagement. A buyer receives only information authorized for the transaction's current stage.

fields.name: Exit-readiness financial and customer evidence
fields.prompt: Define the financial, operational, and customer evidence needed for a credible ownership-transition review. Separate canonical owner profit from any buyer-specific earnings measure, and identify unresolved adjustments without inventing a valuation multiple or sale price.
fields.example: Organize 12 months of reconciled revenue, accepted-fee ledgers, credits, bank collections, churn, concentration, and contractor costs. Present $202,500 as the canonical Base owner net profit, not automatically EBITDA. Document owner duties and replacement-cost assumptions separately. Support retention claims with renewals and client correspondence rather than projected pipeline value.

worksheets.completion_gate: The operator closes the 30-day sprint with documented test results, actual spending, client-acquisition evidence, a funded next-month plan, named pod responsibilities, and an organized operating ledger. Any uncompleted milestone retains an owner, dependency, and review date.
